# vaultwarden Provider

Terraform provider for [Vaultwarden](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden), an unofficial Bitwarden-compatible server. It supports and is tested against the latest two Vaultwarden minor releases, currently 1.36.x and 1.37.x; older Vaultwarden versions get best-effort support only, and the provider warns when it detects one.

The provider authenticates in up to two ways, which can be combined:

- **As a user**, with `email` and `master_password`. Required for resources that act on behalf of a user, such as organizations and collections, because their data is encrypted client-side with the user's keys. If the user has two-step login enabled, also set the user's personal API key (`client_id` and `client_secret`).
- **As the server admin**, with `admin_token`. Required for resources that use the `/admin` API, such as `vaultwarden_user` and `vaultwarden_account_register`. The admin page must be enabled on the server.

Every attribute can also be set with an environment variable.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# User authentication, for organizations, collections and organization users
provider "vaultwarden" {
  endpoint        = "https://vaultwarden.example.com"
  email           = "user@example.com"
  master_password = var.master_password
}

# User authentication with the user's personal API key, when two-step login
# is enabled. The master password is still needed to decrypt the user's keys.
provider "vaultwarden" {
  endpoint        = "https://vaultwarden.example.com"
  email           = "user@example.com"
  master_password = var.master_password
  client_id       = var.client_id
  client_secret   = var.client_secret
}

# Admin authentication, for vaultwarden_user and vaultwarden_account_register.
# It can be combined with user authentication.
provider "vaultwarden" {
  endpoint    = "https://vaultwarden.example.com"
  admin_token = var.admin_token
}

# Every attribute can also be set with an environment variable:
# VAULTWARDEN_ENDPOINT, VAULTWARDEN_EMAIL, VAULTWARDEN_MASTER_PASSWORD,
# VAULTWARDEN_CLIENT_ID, VAULTWARDEN_CLIENT_SECRET, VAULTWARDEN_ADMIN_TOKEN
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `endpoint` (String) The URL of the Vaultwarden server. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

### Optional

- `admin_token` (String, Sensitive) The admin token, for resources that use the `/admin` API. This requires the admin page to be enabled. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_ADMIN_TOKEN` environment variable.
- `client_id` (String) The `client_id` of the user's personal API key, to log in with the API key instead of the master password, for example when two-step login is enabled. Requires `email` and `master_password`. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) The `client_secret` of the user's personal API key. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.
- `email` (String) The email of the user to authenticate as. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_EMAIL` environment variable.
- `master_password` (String, Sensitive) The master password of the user, used to log in and to decrypt the user's keys. Can also be set with the `VAULTWARDEN_MASTER_PASSWORD` environment variable.
